## Two decks with layered video (deck B)

1. Answer Yes when setup asks whether to create a second deck (deck B). Deck B goes on the opposite side of the crossfader (if deck A is `Off`, deck A is set to `Left` and deck B to `Right`). If deck A's preset is "… deck 1" ("(MIDI ch 1)" for CDJs), deck B gets "… deck 2" ("(MIDI ch 2)") of the same model. `Cut-in`, `Fade width` and `Fade curve` start with deck A's values.
2. A video import goes to the deck whose window (the FX window of `scratch engine` or `scratch engine B`) was opened last. If neither window was open, you are asked “Which deck should it go to?” (`Deck A` / `Deck B`). Deck B's video goes on the `video B` track and its audio on the `audio B` track.
3. The video sync script keeps the edit cursor on deck A's position and moves the item on the `video B view` track to deck B's position. That way REAPER's video window shows both decks layered, each at its own frame.
4. For smooth blends, set both decks' `Fade width` to 100%, `Cut-in` to 0 and `Fade curve` to `Equal power` (setup `Crossfader` tab). For scratch cuts, set `Fade width` small (about 2%) and `Fade curve` to `Linear`. By default, it is set in between: `Cut-in` 2%, `Fade width` 30%, and `Fade curve` `Equal power`.
5. Choose the blend or transition with `Video blend` on deck A's setup `Video` tab. With a blend (`Mix` to `Chroma key`), the crossfader at deck A's end shows only A, at deck B's end only B, and in between the chosen blend. With a transition (`Wipe right` and after), the crossfader's position is how far the transition has gone (see “Blends and transitions” for how they look). If both decks' sound is cut, the picture goes black too.

- With deck B, cutting the sound does not mute the `video` track (the picture is faded within the blend instead).
- The Video processor makes video processing heavier (about one CPU core on the PC we tested). Blending and effects are calculated at up to 1280×720, and larger videos are scaled down to that size. Small videos (for example, 320×240) are scaled up to fit within a 960×720 frame while maintaining their aspect ratio before processing, so effect lines and noise do not look coarse. When the project's video size is set to automatic, blending and output use the larger of the two decks' video sizes, scaled to fit within the range of 960×720 to 1280×720. Converting the samples to 720p all-intra keeps it light (on import, videos taller than the height chosen in setup, 720 by default, are offered a downscaling conversion even if they are already all-intra).
- Keep `video B` and `audio B` muted (deck B's picture is shown only through `video B view`). The sync script moves the `video B view` item, so there is no need to move it by hand.
